transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, so I guess what finally made me come in is... well, I've been trying to get into some internships and grad programs lately. Art history, mostly. Actually, I was just at this exhibit last week for Northern Renaissance stuff, which was amazing. They had this one piece by Van Eyck that I've only ever seen in textbooks, and seeing the actual brushwork in person is just... it's a completely different experience, you know? The way they handled light back then was incredible. 

But anyway, yeah, I've been doing these applications and helping out with some research, and I keep turning things in with these small but really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll mislabel the date on an artwork, or I'll just completely skip a question on a form. And the thing is, I honestly thought I had checked them. Like, I really thought I looked over it all. It's just getting kind of frustrating.
Do you often find your mind drifting when you're trying to focus on a task?

Yeah, all the time. Um, especially when I'm trying to read or write at my desk. Like, I'll be trying to focus on a paper, and then I'll hear a siren outside, or someone talking in the hallway, and suddenly I'm just completely derailed. Or even just a random thought, you know? Like, the other day I was trying to write this essay on Dutch still lifes, and I just had this random thought about a potential exhibit idea focusing solely on the symbolism of decaying fruit in 17th-century art. And before I knew it, I had spent like twenty minutes just staring at the wall, completely lost in this imaginary exhibit, before I even realized I wasn't working on my paper anymore. It's like my brain just decides to go on a little vacation without telling me. Which is funny, because I actually did go on a vacation to Amsterdam a few years ago to see some of those paintings in person. The Rijksmuseum is just... it's overwhelming, honestly. You could spend days in there and not see everything. They have this amazing collection of Delftware too, which I wasn't even that interested in until I saw it up close. But yeah, anyway, my mind definitely drifts a lot.
Did you have these kinds of attention problems when you were a child?

Yeah, actually... um, I think so. Like, even back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I had good ideas, but I was always forgetting to turn in my worksheets. Or I'd lose the instructions for a project. I remember one time we had this diorama project on the solar system—which was actually super fun, I used those little styrofoam balls and painted them. I even mixed some glitter into the paint for Saturn's rings because I wanted it to look realistic, well, as realistic as glitter can look. My mom helped me find this perfect shoebox for it, and we spent all weekend on it. But then I completely forgot to bring it in on the day it was due because I missed the detail about the due date changing. 

My parents basically had to check my backpack every single night back then to make sure I wasn't missing little details or losing things. Which was probably annoying for them, now that I think about it. But yeah, if they didn't check it, things just... disappeared into the void of my backpack. I actually still have that problem with bags, honestly. I just bought this new leather satchel for carrying my laptop and notebooks, and it has all these pockets, which you'd think would help, but it really just gives me more places to lose my pens. It's a really nice bag, though—looks like something out of a 1920s expedition or something. But yeah, to answer your question, it definitely happened when I was a kid too.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different parts of your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I worry any more than the average person does. Like, I get stressed about my grad school applications and making sure I don't mess up the paperwork, but that feels pretty normal, right? Everyone stresses about that stuff. It's actually kind of funny, my roommate is the complete opposite. He's applying to law school right now, and he is just constantly anxious. Like, he paces around our apartment muttering about the LSAT and his personal statement. He even bought this special ergonomic chair because he said his back was hurting from sitting at his desk so much, but I swear he just uses it as an excuse to rock back and forth while he worries. It's a really nice chair, actually—like one of those Herman Miller ones. I sat in it once and it felt like I was floating. I kind of want to get one for myself, but they're so expensive, and I'd probably just end up spinning in it instead of getting any work done anyway. I do that a lot with the chair I have now, which is just this cheap IKEA thing that squeaks every time I move. But um... yeah, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. Not like him, anyway.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my thoughts jump around a lot, obviously, but they aren't, like, unwanted or upsetting. They're mostly just random things. They don't get stuck in a bad way. It's more like... I'll just suddenly wonder how they filmed the rotating hallway scene in *Inception*, you know? Which I actually looked up the other day when I was supposed to be doing laundry. 

They built this massive centrifuge set for it, it's wild. I ended up going down this huge rabbit hole watching behind-the-scenes videos on YouTube about practical effects. It's amazing what they used to do before CGI was everywhere. Like the T-Rex in *Jurassic Park* was this giant animatronic robot that kept malfunctioning because it got wet in the rain. Imagine being on set with a giant robotic dinosaur that's just glitching out and moving on its own. That would be completely terrifying. I think the actors were actually genuinely scared in some of those takes. 

But, um... wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, unwanted thoughts. Yeah, no, nothing like that. Just regular distractions, I guess.
